newsitem.title: JAPAN: Group urges Japan banks to beef up compliance.
newsitem.headline: Group urges Japan banks to beef up compliance.

text.p: Japanese banks need to beef up their legal compliance ahead of planned "Big Bang" financial reforms, the Federation of Bankers Associations of Japan said in a statement on Tuesday.
The industry group said it would also come up with a code of moral conduct aimed at restoring confidence in the banking industry and setting out the social responsibilities of banks.

The unusual move by the group follows a high-profile scandal involving one of Japan's top commercial banks, the Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB), and the nation's biggest brokerage, Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
Former DKB executives have been indicted on charges of making illegal loans to a "sokaiya" corporate racketeer in violation of the nation's Commercial Code.
Sokaiya extort money from companies by threatening to disclose management misdeeds or disrupt annual shareholders meetings. Payoffs to the corporate extortionists have been illegal since 1983.
In Tuesday's statement, the federation said that each bank should have strong enough corporate ethics to reject such actions.
To enhance the transparency of bank management, they should also improve disclosure, it said.
